correctness.rationale: For every n>=6, KG(n,2) has diameter two and at least three common neighbors for any nonadjacent pair, hence is 3-connected. KG(6,2) has 45 edges on 15 vertices and is nonplanar; all larger graphs contain it. Ko–Park Theorem 3.16 gives the rank of unordered configuration H1; a natural equivariant map onto graph H1 is proved surjective using fundamental cycles of length at most five with a parked second particle. Exact signed formulas on 0-,1-,2-cubes and equivariant Euler–Poincaré yield the universal trace. For n=6 the standalone checker constructs 105/585/765 cubical cells, checks d1d2=0, ranks d2 modulo 3 and 2 as 450 and 449, agrees on all 720 signed group actions, and independently computes the eleven Specht multiplicities; n=7 checks all fifteen class types. Integral H2 is free as the kernel of a homomorphism of free 2-chains with no 3-chains. No finite experiment substitutes for the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed novelty is exclusively the natural all-n degree-two symmetric-group character and n=6 Specht decomposition. Ko–Park supplies the previously known non-equivariant rank and exchange torsion, and Farber–Hanbury supplies graph-configuration background. Relevant indexed literature Kneser data concern Lovász neighborhood or Čech complexes, and the nearest unordered-configuration representation concerns the Petersen KG(5,2). None of the materially checked named results asserts the all-n character or the nine-type 315-dimensional decomposition. A universal equivalence or unindexed calculation may exist and is identified as residual risk.
residual_risks: Indexed indexed literature linked full originals on Kneser/graph braid topics were not accessible; comparisons involving them are limited to distinct-object summaries, not whole-document negative assertions.
An unindexed or unpublished representation-theoretic study of Kneser graph braid homology may already contain an equivalent all-n character.
A more general equivariant theorem beyond those inspected could imply the full calculation, although ordinary Betti formulas alone do not.

value.rationale: The two-subset Kneser graphs form a canonical, coordinate-symmetric sequence; n=6 is the first triangle-bearing member after Petersen. The exact, uniform automorphism character detects nine irreducible symmetry types in 315-dimensional H2, gives a nontrivial A6-fixed-space vanishing, and avoids constructing rapidly growing configuration chain matrices. This identifies a natural complete equivariant invariant beyond known nonequivariant ranks, with reproducible conjugacy-class data and future extension to symmetry quotients.
